objective: Prove, for tori of every shape of the square, triangular and honeycomb lattices of rule-60 rings with equally spaced contacts: the systole lemma of PLAIN-TIME-20261108-001B holds for every cover, in particular for the tube T/<v> of one lattice vector; the square tube of (2,1) and the triangular tube of a vector of length sqrt 3 are on time, and so is every torus holding such a vector (two square tori of index 3 excepted); the mirror tube of (1,2) is late; every other tube of a short vector is late; and hence a torus is on time exactly when it holds a rotation of (2,0) or (2,1) (square) or a vector of length sqrt 3 (triangular), or is one of finitely many listed tori of small index.
status: Proved 2026-11-09 (Theorem 1 by hand; Theorem 2 by hand for the square tube and by a checked certificate for the triangular tube; Theorem 3 with an exact census below explicit index bounds): the systole lemma holds for every cover; the square tube of (2,1) and the triangular tube of a vector of length sqrt 3 are on time, with unique shortest routes at every closest contact, and so is every torus holding such a vector (two square tori of index 3 excepted), while the mirror tube of (1,2) is late at distance 4; so a square torus is on time exactly when it holds a rotation of (2,0) or (2,1) or is one of 23 listed tori of index 5 to 17, a triangular torus when it holds a vector of length sqrt 3 or is one of 85 listed tori of index 4 to 21, and a honeycomb torus only when it is one of 15 listed tori of index 1 to 9.
title: Short loops rescue late rings: every torus that reads distance plainly
